summary.text: A previously healthy 61-year-old man was transferred with 10 days of recurrent fever and 4 days of orthopnea and oliguria after sitting on a lawn about 20 days earlier. He had a crusted ulcerative scrotal lesion, a diffuse maculopapular rash, bilateral crackles, elevated CRP and creatinine, multifocal lung haziness and focal hypokinesis on echocardiography. Scrub typhus was diagnosed clinically and intravenous azithromycin was started.

On hospital day 3 pneumonic infiltration worsened and cefepime was started for hospital-acquired pneumonia; oxygen demand and renal dysfunction then increased and a cardiac arrest followed, resuscitated with 25 minutes of CPR, with ventilation and renal replacement started in the ICU. Next day troponin I rose further and echocardiography showed global hypokinesis; endomyocardial biopsy and coronary angiography followed, and angiography showed no significant lesion.

Before ICU transfer he became bradycardic and hypotensive and had a second, pulseless electrical activity arrest needing extracorporeal CPR with femoral VA-ECMO cannulation. Echocardiography then showed thickened ventricular walls and a new pericardial effusion; left atrial cannulation via septostomy relieved refractory pulmonary edema. Whole-blood PCR identified the Ikeda strain and the biopsy showed T-lymphocytic myocarditis, confirming acute fulminant myocarditis from scrub typhus; no immunomodulators were given.

Cardiac function recovered and he was weaned from ECMO and the ventilator. Global aphasia with a normal brain MRI and lymphocytic CSF pleocytosis suggested meningoencephalitis; doxycycline was added and the aphasia resolved three days later. Antibody converted positive on hospital day 19, and he was discharged after about 10 days on the ward with an echocardiographic ejection fraction of 54% and cardioprotective drugs.

article_limitations: Caption-layer visual status not_inspected; the 4 article JPEGs and the supplementary figure were inspected in separate visual and supplement submissions.

Supplementary Table 1 (laboratory findings) and the echocardiography videos are reviewed under the supplement sidecars, not copied into article-text facts.
No hospital-day dates are stated for several events (arrests, ECMO); order is given only where the text states it.
The Supplementary Figure 1 legend and the case text disagree on the hospital day of the T wave inversion; the day is left out of that item.
Discussion statements about incidence, mortality, strain virulence and literature are background, not patient facts.

Supplementary Table 1 conflicts with the case text on the troponin T reference interval and the white blood cell unit; the text facts are review_only source conflicts, and the matching SM2 rows must be too.
Supplementary Videos 1 and 2 (WMV) were not machine-typed as video by the acquisition tool; their manifest rows rest on caption and filename, although decoded frames were viewed.
